rv.q: Another unearthed gem from Mint Theater, Crooked Cross proves that our present social discontent is nothing new, which is hardly reassuring.
This one is almost too close to the bone.
Ultimately, the bigness of the play's themes and passions are stifled by the conflicting theatrics.
“Crooked Cross” the play is more of a historical curiosity.

While Crooked Cross holds a historic role in predicting the rise of Nazism in an ordinary German family, its low-key development undercuts the drama inherent in the story and seems to evolve too slowly for its own good.
Unfortunately, Crooked Cross makes more of an impression by its timeliness than by its dramatic art.
Although the Mint’s production does not serve the play adequately, Crooked Cross remains a noteworthy work with a message likely to give some theatergoers shivers of recognition.
This is strong stuff, and the cast is up to the task...
Thanks to Carson's compelling script and Bank's crisp direction, which keeps the action flowing, one can see where the characters are headed.

cn.t: Mint Theater's revival of Carson's prescient 1935 warning about fascism's rise earns mixed reviews. Critics praise its historical relevance and timely resonance, though some find the adaptation dramatically uneven and overly cut.
